text:
The only prime that allows the polynomial  
\(x^{2p} - 2p\,x^{m} - p^{2}x^{n} - 1\) to factor over \(\mathbb{Z}[x]\) under the given constraints is \(p=2\).  
For \(p=2\) the admissible pairs \((m,n)\) (with \(n\) odd, \(m\neq n\) and \(m,n<2p=4\)) are  

\[
( m,n ) = (2,1),\;(3,1),\;(1,3),\;(2,3),
\]

and each yields a reducible quartic, e.g.  

\[
\begin{aligned}
x^{4}-4x^{2}-4x-1 &= (x^{2}+2x+1)(x^{2}-2x-1),\\
x^{4}-4x^{3}-4x-1 &= (x^{2}+1)(x^{2}-4x-1),\\
x^{4}-4x-4x^{3}-1 &= (x+1)(x^{3}-5x^{2}+x-1),\\
x^{4}-4x^{2}-4x^{3}-1 &= (x+1)(x^{3}-5x^{2}+x-1).
\end{aligned}
\]

Summing \(p+m+n\) over these four admissible triples gives  

\[
(2+2+1)+(2+3+1)+(2+1+3)+(2+2+3)=5+6+6+7=24.
\]

**ANSWER: 24**
